stocks.note: Numbers as of market close on May 13th.
stocks.news: Kevin Warsh confirmed as new Fed Chair. Powell's last day as Chair is tomorrow, though he stays on as a Fed Governor. Warsh was a Fed Governor from 2006-2011 with a well-known hawkish track record. The institutional pivot we've been tracking just became structural. Jensen Huang of Nvidia (NVDA +2.29%) was added last-minute to Trump's China delegation. U.S. rules have blocked Nvidia's top AI chips from China for almost four years. A deal could change that, and the market is pricing the option. Google (GOOG +3.97%) is going hard on data centers, $200B planned this year, with some potentially space-based. SpaceX is reportedly heading for an IPO at a $2T valuation. The AI capex flywheel keeps accelerating. The flip side: Walmart (WMT +0.86%) and Microsoft's LinkedIn (MSFT -0.63%) both announced layoffs to pivot toward AI. Cisco (CSCO +2.60%) beat earnings and immediately announced 4,000 job cuts. Block, Meta, Palantir all on the same trajectory. AI is paying for itself out of headcount.

economy.note: US 10-Year and Gold as of 4:00 PM ET May 13th; WTI Crude reflects today's intraday move via investing.com.
economy.commentary:
The big macro story: April PPI just printed and it is worse than April CPI. Producer prices jumped 1.4% month-over-month, the biggest monthly increase in over four years. Annual PPI hit 6.0%, the highest since 2022. The chart above shows the spike. That is the wholesale-prices side of the same Iran-oil and tariff story that pushed CPI to 3.8% on Tuesday. PPI tends to lead CPI, so the next CPI print is unlikely to cool.

The market repricing: Wall Street now sees a 39% chance the Fed HIKES rates this year, not cuts. A week ago that number was near zero. Combined with Warsh replacing Powell as Fed Chair tomorrow, the rate environment for the next six months has been completely re-priced.

The 10-year held at 4.46% (-0.01%), gold cooled to $4,695, and WTI pulled back to $100.36 (-0.65%) but Brent held at $105.67. The energy premium continues to feed the inflation tape. France's unemployment jumped to 8.1% (highest since 2021), so the global growth picture is softening even as inflation runs. That is the stagflation worry the bond market is starting to price.

crypto.note: Numbers as of 4:00 PM ET on May 13th.
crypto.commentary: Bitcoin slipped under $80K to $79,565 (+0.35% intraday recovery), ETH at $2,263, XRP at $1.43. The notable story: crypto IPOs are pausing. Ledger, the hardware wallet maker valued near $4B, just halted its planned U.S. IPO, citing market conditions. Kraken paused earlier this year. The CLARITY Act friction we covered yesterday is now showing up in capital markets, the regulatory tailwind crypto firms were pricing in for IPO timing has reversed. XRP just topped BTC and ETH in 24-hour volume on the two biggest South Korean exchanges, $150M moved. Korean retail historically front-runs broader market moves, so it is a flag worth watching.

real_estate.homebuilder: PPI Hits 6%, Warsh Replaces Powell, And Buyers Still Bought At 6.57%
real_estate.commentary:
Three threads to anchor client conversations.

First, the counter-narrative buyers need to hear: MBA purchase applications rose 4% week-over-week and 7% year-over-year, even as the 30-year mortgage rate hit its highest point in five weeks. Less Iran optimism and hot April inflation pushed bond yields up; mortgage rates followed. Buyers bought anyway. That is the data point that disarms the "I'm waiting for rates to drop" client. They are not just waiting, they are getting passed by the buyers who are transacting.

Second, the Fed-Chair changeover matters more than the market is pricing. Powell's last day as Chair is tomorrow. Kevin Warsh, the incoming Chair, was the hawk on the FOMC during 2006-2011, famously dissenting against more aggressive easing post-crisis. He is taking over with PPI at 6%, CPI at 3.8%, and Wall Street now giving a 39% chance to a Fed HIKE this year. The "rates fall in 2026" thesis is officially dead. Repeat that to every fence-sitter on your roster.

Third, the Hamptons softening signal. Rental rates there are down 2.5% year-over-year just before the U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills (150,000 visitors). Last year's gold rush flooded supply, this year's market is absorbing the overhang. The lesson for Bay Area listing agents: when a tier sees a sudden supply pulse, prices recalibrate within months. Watch your local inventory closely. Today's number is up.

Total active inventory across the 15-city board is 2,902, up 49 from Wednesday, the first material inventory rise this week. 216 new listings today, slightly above yesterday's 211. 243 closed sales for the week, up 3 from yesterday. Inventory is loading and deals are still pushing through. The fast pulse is in Danville (24) and Hayward bouncing back to 10.

For listing agents: with inventory rising and the rate ceiling now looking sticky, today is the day to pull the trigger on any pricing conversations you have been deferring. Your competitive position erodes the longer you wait. The MBA purchase-app data tells you buyers are out there. The PPI and Warsh narrative tells you they are not going to be helped by waiting either, so neither are you.

For buyer agents: this is the call to make today. Purchase applications up 7% YoY at five-week-high rates means the buyer pool is committed. Walk your fence-sitters through the rate-trend math one more time. Cuts are off the table. The buyer in escrow today is the one who paid the bottom of this cycle.
